content: 1. Administering secretin intravenously at a dose of 2 mcg/kg over one minute has not been established as safe or effective. 2. Atropine reduces the effects of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use of anticholinergic drugs, such as atropine, may result in a diminished response to secretin during stimulation testing. Discontinue anticholinergic drugs at least five half-lives before administering secretin. 3. Benzotropine also decreases the effects of secretin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Similar to atropine, concurrent use of anticholinergic drugs may lead to a hyporesponse to secretin stimulation testing. Discontinue anticholinergic drugs at least five half-lives prior to secretin administration. 4. Cimetidine, an H2-receptor antagonist, may cause an exaggerated gastrin secretion response during secretin stimulation testing, potentially leading to a false diagnosis of gastrinoma. Discontinue H2-receptor antagonists at least two days before administering secretin to improve diagnostic accuracy for gastrinoma. 5.
